title: I use AI as a coach and it still makes mistakes.
author: Thesirrob
selftext: First, let me say that AI has helped me become a decent trader. I am profitable for the first time because I keep refining my prompts. I have been creating prompts for trading for years. I use it to analyze my charts and help me filter out noise. I would not be the trader I am today, without AI. With that being said, do not solely rely on it to trade for you. YOU WILL LOSE. I am not saying that because it lost because of it, I am actually giving it credit for helping spot the mistakes it makes. Even with the detailed prompts I have, it still makes mistakes that my eyes would see easily. There is no program, no bot, no algorithm that will make you profitable without you understanding the charts on a higher level. If you're reading this post, you're probably already better than most people trying to trade. If you're on Reddit looking up trading, you're already in the higher percentage of people that are willing to put the work in. Use AI as a tool, don't blow your account relying on bot, signals or whatever. Give your more credit, you're better than you believe.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the mistakes your eyes catch easily are the telling ones. a model's chart read comes back in the same sure tone whether it's right or wrong, so rereading the good calls tells you nothing, you have to count all of them. Quantradin keeps that count. I built it this summer: you plug in your own AI and its stock calls run on pretend money, so a wrong one costs nothing. quantradin.com. which mistake does yours repeat most?

comments.author: k1_r1
comments.body: agree with this. the mistakes are worst when you cant check them, and a chart read is basically uncheckable in the moment. what helped me was making the ai write the setup down as rules instead of giving me reads, then backtesting the rules, so its mistakes show up in the numbers instead of in my account. i work on portfoliolab which is built around that loop, you describe the setup, it codes and tests it, then you can paper trade it. but your main point stands, if you dont understand what its testing the tool cant save you

comments.author: Square-Middle-4474
comments.body: Forgive me for taking the opposite side. I hesitate to say that I train people to use AI (but that is part of what I do) and I can tell you that most of the problems AI user make are related to **not knowing how to prompt.** There are several ways to learn. Don't approach me, the mods for some reason won't allow me to help you any more than that.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
The mistakes your eyes catch easily are worth tracking on purpose. Keep a simple log for each trade: what the AI said about the chart, what you decided, and how it went. After 50 or so trades you'll see whether it's really filtering noise or mostly agreeing with you.

Also, the same chart and prompt can get a different answer on a second try. If you run it twice and the read flips, that's probably a setup to skip rather than trust.

Since you keep refining prompts, save which version you used on each trade too. Otherwise it's hard to tell later if you got better or the prompt did.

comments.author: Individual-Quote-958
comments.body: Treating it as a tool and not the decider is the right call. One thing that helps is logging every time you disagree with its read and checking a week later who was right. After a month you know where it's actually weak instead of guessing, and you can stop asking it about those setups. Chart reads from screenshots seem to be the weakest spot for most models, so I'd lean on it more for reviewing your trade notes.
